The course starts with one question: **what has this stage actually produced?**
You will author source identity, choose a physical model, prepare real backend
inputs, execute explicitly on a solver host and read the complete return in a
fresh session. Optional EPR reanalysis changes attributed assumptions on actual
recorded evidence. No page supplies synthetic solver output or runs a solver
during site rendering.

These lessons describe accepted V1 behavior; the lessons themselves are not proof
of numerical accuracy. The [support matrix](backend-support.qmd) records
capabilities and evidence limits. Executable public component notebooks remain
owned by OrPen SC PDK; SCGSim owns the APIs and explanations they use.

## Mainline: from source to an interpretable return

| Lesson | What you do | What you retain |
|---|---|---|
| [1. Choose an environment](course/installation.qmd) | Separate preparation, native host and analysis dependencies | Matching package/source identity and a selected kernel |
| [2. Author shared Xmon inputs](tutorial-xmon-input.qmd) | Register occurrences, assign final Nets and prepare GeometryPlan | One immutable source snapshot |
| [3. Inspect and retain source](course/source-observations.qmd) | Read normalized inputs and save the paired source | Source facts, unknowns and GDS/stack identity |
| Choose a backend below | Configure its physical model and request | Actual mesh/config or portable AEDT handoff |
| [4. Inspect the prepared backend](course/solver-observations.qmd) | Optionally inspect bound mesh/native assignments | Stage-specific geometry evidence, not a solve |
| [5. Execute on the host](course/execute.qmd) | Transfer and launch the complete handoff explicitly | Actual returned receipt, outputs and logs |
| [6. Restart and resolve](course/returned-results.qmd) | Verify the full return before reading physics | Identity-bound native quantities and benchmark availability |
| [7. Reanalyze EPR offline](course/offline-epr.qmd) | Change assumptions on an available recorded EPR result | New attributed analysis, same field evidence |

Lessons 2–3 share one preparation session and `snapshot`. Backend lessons state
which variables they need. Lesson 6 deliberately starts a fresh session and
uses preserved files rather than the earlier live objects. You can start there
when a complete returned package already exists. Ordinary network/extraction
work ends with its verified native result; EPR stages apply only to a result
that actually contains the required fields and requested analysis.

## Choose the physical question

| Question | Backend lesson | Source prerequisite |
|---|---|---|
| Terminal capacitance with explicit conductor/exterior ground choices | [Palace Electrostatic](course/palace-electrostatic.qmd) | Shared snapshot |
| Resonant modes without optional film/port requests | [Palace Eigenmode](course/palace-eigenmode.qmd) | Shared snapshot |
| Surface/bulk and inductive-port participation | [Palace Xmon EPR](tutorial-xmon-palace.qmd) | Shared Xmon + ordinary Eigenmode stages |
| Port-free CPW mode frequency/native Q | [Ordinary HFSS Eigenmode](course/aedt-eigenmode.qmd) | [CPW GDS/material mapping](course/aedt-inputs.qmd) |
| Surface/bulk/junction EPR with source-linked topology | [AEDT Xmon EPR](tutorial-xmon-aedt.qmd) | Shared Xmon snapshot |
| Final fields on a released, sealed solution | [AEDT saved-field analysis](course/aedt-saved-fields.qmd) | Complete returned EPR cohort; native host still required |
| Two-port response with integration lines | [HFSS Driven Modal](course/aedt-driven-modal.qmd) | CPW GDS/material mapping |
| Two-port response with reference conductors | [HFSS Driven Terminal](course/aedt-driven-terminal.qmd) | CPW GDS/material mapping |
| Finite 3D conductor matrices | [Q3D](course/aedt-q3d.qmd) | CPW GDS with finite metal import interval |
| Per-unit-length cross-section C/G/L/R | [Q2D](course/aedt-q2d.qmd) | Explicit rectangles and conductor groups |

The CPW lessons share one source lesson instead of repeating the specimen in
each family. Q2D uses explicit cross-section facts, not an implicit slice of a
GeometryPlan. A common package lifecycle does not flatten capacitance,
frequency, S-parameters, participation or per-unit-length quantities into a
single physical result.

## Matched public inputs {#public-inputs}

The public inputs below are pinned to OrPen source
[`35b4dc1cdd3f921badcac2fe57a98366315ae8d9`](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk/tree/35b4dc1cdd3f921badcac2fe57a98366315ae8d9),
which declares OrPen `0.1.0` and GDSFactory 9.48.x. Resolve its dependencies
with the SCGSim checkout described by the selected documentation build. These
lessons have been reconstructed against the current SCGSim APIs; the former
`a0e179ab`/`dev28` tutorial checkpoint is historical, not their API authority.

| Canonical public notebook group | Use |
|---|---|
| [Kosen2024_Xmon](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk/tree/35b4dc1cdd3f921badcac2fe57a98366315ae8d9/notebooks/src/ComponentSimulation/Kosen2024_Xmon) | Palace Route A/B Electrostatic/Eigenmode and source-first Xmon studies |
| [ComponentSimulation/CpwFiniteGround](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk/tree/35b4dc1cdd3f921badcac2fe57a98366315ae8d9/notebooks/src/ComponentSimulation/CpwFiniteGround) | Ordinary HFSS Eigenmode, Driven Modal/Terminal and Q3D |
| [CrossSectionSimulation/CpwFiniteGround](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk/tree/35b4dc1cdd3f921badcac2fe57a98366315ae8d9/notebooks/src/CrossSectionSimulation/CpwFiniteGround) | Q2D rectangles and conductor groups |

The specimen dimensions and presets are public model inputs, not measured
process/device evidence. An old notebook's comments do not replace the current
package contract: for example, 3D Region padding uses the native
`(+X,-X,+Y,-Y,+Z,-Z)` order, while Q2D uses `(-X,+X,-Y,+Y)`.

## Read deeper when the stage needs it

[Geometry concepts](concepts/geometry.qmd) explain source identity and
approximation. [EPR concepts](eigenmode-epr.qmd) explain energy, normalization,
mask alternatives and loss unknowns. The Contract navigation holds exact
interfaces and failure rules; [architecture](architecture.qmd) describes their
implementation. Start with [installation](course/installation.qmd).
